content.text:
Components Found

- `funder_alias_links`: compares every stored canonical name and alias using lowercase + collapsed whitespace + trimming; equality creates an undirected connection between distinct funders. No fuzzy or company-number matching here. [Migration](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/db/migrations/20261012170746_funder_alias_groups.up.sql:1)
- `funder_family_names` / `funder_family_links`: explicit reviewed BBC, GB News, and Premier League name lists; canonical funder names matching that normalization receive their family’s edges. [Migration](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/db/migrations/20261012173107_reviewed_funder_families.up.sql:1)
- `funder_alias_groups`: union of alias edges and reviewed-family edges, recursively traversed into connected components. [Combined grouping](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/db/migrations/20261012173107_reviewed_funder_families.up.sql:36)
- Search repository consumes groups; details repository exposes members and connection evidence and aggregates funding. [Search](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder.rs:37), [Details](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/entity_details.rs:105)

Flow

1. Existing canonical names and aliases produce exact normalized alias links. Curated family memberships produce additional links.
2. The recursive view makes edges bidirectional and traverses them transitively. If A shares an alias with B, and B belongs to a reviewed family with C, all three join one component.
3. Each component’s representative ID is `min(member_id::text)::uuid`; isolated funders represent themselves. The representative’s stored name and kind become the search result’s name/kind. [Representative selection](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/db/migrations/20261012173107_reviewed_funder_families.up.sql:41)
4. Text search first finds and scores individual funder names/aliases with PostgreSQL `word_similarity`; then selects the highest-scoring qualifying member per group, emitting only one result per representative ID. A match on another member’s canonical name is reported as `SearchMatchSource::Alias`, preserving the matched text. [Scoring and grouping](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder.rs:39)
5. Individual-name phonetic fallback also deduplicates by group, ranking by edit distance, similarity, then source ID. [Phonetic grouping](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder.rs:115)
6. Details lookup accepts any member ID. Within one repeatable-read transaction it gathers representative label/kind, all canonical names and aliases, member IDs, alias-link evidence, and reviewed-family evidence. [Profile lookup](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/entity_details.rs:109)
7. Funding entries for every member ID are aggregated by parliamentary member and currency. The service summarizes these allocations into currency and party totals. [SQL aggregation](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/entity_details.rs:197), [Service summary](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/domain/services/entity_details.rs:158)
8. HTTP serialization exposes `aliases`, `member_ids`, `alias_links`, and `family_links`; alias edges retain normalized and original matching names, family edges retain the reviewed key and original canonical names. [API fields](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/handlers/entity_details.rs:191)

Boundaries

- This is a search/detail grouping layer over stored funders; the migrations do not rewrite funder IDs or funding-entry ownership.
- Search similarity determines which component matches a query; exact equality and reviewed family edges determine component membership.
- Family matching uses canonical names only; aliases can bring additional entities into the family transitively.
- SQLx queries own persistence traversal; the service owns summary construction; the HTTP adapter serializes provenance.

Non-Obvious Things

- Representative choice is mechanical UUID ordering, not a preferred organization name, most frequent name, or strongest identity evidence.
- Since these are ordinary views, changes to names/aliases immediately change groups; adding an entity with a smaller UUID can change the representative.
- Alias equality has no funder-kind guard, company-number requirement, or ambiguity check. Any nonempty normalized shared name connects funders.
- The details `company_number` is present only when the group has exactly one distinct non-null number; several members may lack a number. Conflicting numbers suppress the field rather than preventing grouping. [Company number rule](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/entity_details.rs:114)
- A details request using a nonrepresentative ID returns that requested ID but the representative’s name/kind, because profile construction uses `Funder::new(id, row.funder_name, kind)`. [Construction](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/entity_details.rs:189)
- Funding aggregation sums entries without deduplicating declaration IDs; provenance remains available as group membership and graph edges.

Files Read

The two grouping migrations, `outbound/funder.rs`, `outbound/entity_details.rs`, `domain/services/entity_details.rs`, and `inbound/http/handlers/entity_details.rs`; searched `domain/services/entity_search.rs` and HTTP search serialization for match-source handling.

Open Questions

- Is retaining a requested nonrepresentative ID with a representative label intentional?
- Are reviewed families meant to represent a legal entity or a broader reporting organization? The BBC list explicitly spans multiple named organizations.
- Is shared-name equality acceptable for ambiguous individuals? The grouping layer itself does not distinguish them.
